meta.description: Quantifies protein abundance from mass spectrometry peptide, PSM, and reporter signals using LFQ, TMT/iTRAQ, SILAC, AP-MS, MSstats, iq MaxLFQ, sample loading, and IRS normalization.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md
meta.environment: mass-spec-proteomics-analyst: R 4.4.3 via r.sh, Python 3.12 shared venv. No package or source changes were made.

scientific_integrity.detail: All checked numerical claims matched persisted outputs; no fabricated data or citations were introduced.

practice_boundaries.detail: The source explicitly routes patient classification and treatment decisions to validated clinical assays; Input 6 was correctly a refusal-only boundary test.

methodological_ground.detail: The Skill distinguishes normalization from summarization, does not normalize AP-MS as balanced proteome data, and correctly treats TMT compression as physical.

code_usability.detail: In the specified audit environment, the central MSstats and MSnbase routes produce asserted files but terminate with exit 11. The minimal probes also exit 11 after loading MSstats, MSnbase, or Arrow; base R exits 0. A compatible compiled R package set is required for runnable deployment.

functional_suitability.note: All stated quantification families have present source files and runnable logic; live use is constrained by the R ABI fault recorded separately.

reliability.note: Input guards, noninteractive impurity correction, explicit unbridged references, and AP-MS dead-control reporting are strong, but key documented R workflows do not terminate cleanly in the required environment.

performance_context.note: The core file uses references and scripts for specialized paths; the tested Python and iq routes finish promptly.

agent_usability.note: Clear method selection, error prevention, and scope routing; expected clean-exit behavior is not documented for the affected R stack.

human_usability.note: Natural triggers and strict scientific input handling are appropriate for a data-analysis skill.

security.note: No secrets, network calls, raw shell execution, or destructive operations; column-name validation remains caller-dependent.

maintainability.note: SILAC, AP-MS, MSstats, MaxLFQ, TMT, and example responsibilities are separated into focused files with asserted examples.

agent_specific.note: Precise triggers, progressive disclosure, explicit handoffs, repeatable seeded examples, and clinical/experimental escape hatches are present.

key_strengths: The Phase-1 SILAC repair correctly isolates Pro-free peptide signal and exposes fallback metadata.
AP-MS scoring correctly uses negative-control IPs, rejects all-empty controls, and reports excluded dead controls.
MaxLFQ, IRS, and the shipped example have strong deterministic, persisted-output evidence.
TMT10 and TMTpro calculations produce valid nonnegative matrices before the environment teardown failure.

recommendations.title: Repair the R compiled-package ABI before deployment
recommendations.problem: Core R workflows persist valid outputs but terminate with exit 11 in the specified environment, failing operational stability and code-usability gates.
recommendations.root_cause: The audit R library has incompatible compiled components; Phase 1 identified mzR built against Rcpp 1.0.13 while Rcpp 1.1.1 is installed, and a private mzR source build lacks boost/regex/v4/regex.hpp.
recommendations.fix: Provision an isolated R 4.4.3 library with mutually compatible Rcpp, mzR, MSnbase, MSstats, and Arrow binaries or complete the approved source-build prerequisites. Re-run Inputs 1, 4, 8, and 9 and require clean exit 0 before deployment.
